claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the new characters, such as the Regent and the Necrobinder, for adding fresh playstyles and variety.

citations.review_text: Whilst it has the rough edges of an early access release, there already is a staggering amount of content to dig into. It's simply a better and more expansive version of the original. Plus, the inclusion of multiplayer is such a pleasant surprise; it fits into this game seamlessly.
Very similar to the first game. The new playable characters are a highlight, they're distinct, interesting and well worth a play through

Pretty fun so far. I was expecting more new characters, though, instead of 3 characters from the original. I at least wish they brought over The Watcher since that character felt so unique. The Defect is a cool character, but I wish they just swapped them out for a new character or something. It also feels a bit too similar to the first game, at least so far, I haven't played a ton of the game yet, and I have over 100 hours in the original. I was just expecting it to feel a lot different, I guess. However, that doesn't mean I am not enjoying it, and I intend on playing more. I'll probably update this review later, either when I have more hours, or when it comes out of early access.

My thoughts on the new characters:

The Necrobinder is a pretty sick new character. I really find the summon aspect with Otsy really interesting gameplay wise. Also, the doom mechanic is really cool and can lead to some dope builds. I have had tons of fun with them with the few runs I've done.

I only did one run as The Regent, and I'm not sure how to feel about them. They seem to have interesting mechanics, but I was a little underwhelmed by this new character.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features placeholder art, which some describe as MS paint style.

citations.review_text: Currently addicted. I had STS1 on all platforms I could possibly have it on, so I was super excited to finally get STS2. Equally addicting. I don't particularly enjoy playing the Regent, and the doom mechanic doesn't feel great, but you win some you lose some playing a game in early access. Heavily enjoying the placeholder art in the early access epochs as well, so happy they didn't use AI slop placeholders or something like that. I love these games so much, absolutely worth it even in early access.
Spent more time in MS paint than then the game itself. Please add a colour palette, vector drawing and layers next :)

The characters designs are excellent, the decks are distinct without feeling alien in the fundamental mechanics, and the aesthetics are immaculate (other than the MS paint art that shows up in a few places, but I find that quite charming as an exception to the rule, and I assume they're just early-access placeholders anyway).

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as heavily reliant on RNG and note balance issues regarding enemy damage, health, and status debuffs.

citations.review_text: If you're a fan of terrible RNG, this is the game for you. RNG cards, enemies, maps, RNG everything. Balancing is also a mess. Graphics are good and the gameplay loop can feel addicting but with the RNG and balancing issues make the time put in feel pointless.

At the moment I cannot recommend this game for anyone looking for a casual pastime. Slay the Spire 1 was not perfect, but I felt that it struck a fairly good balance - providing a reasonable challenge while still allowing you to skew your deck towards specialised builds, and most importantly it was possible to make the vast majority of builds 'work' against all bosses and elites (provided you were careful to round out your deck with a few utility cards). 

The same cannot be said for Slay the Spire 2. There are countless negative reviews from players far more skilled than me about the neuances of the way in which certain bosses and elites make it completely impossible to win unless you were lucky enough (and I stress the word lucky here) to have been offered the required cards to protect against their specific gimmic. For example - if you dont happen to see any ways to remove cards from your deck, and dont have very high damage output, you will simply lose to any of the elites that put overwhelming numbers of debuff cards into your hand and deck. I would not have an issue with this if I had been offered the methods to counter it, which I had not taken, or if the elites that hard counter specific builds were a rare ocurrence (or they only appeared in the later floors to give you time to build up a defence). But they are frequent, they are varied in what they target (good luck guessing which ones to account for on any particular run), they come at you early in the run, and they are so targeted at a particular win condition that the game essentially punishes you for guessing wrong. It is not fun to lose when I dont have a sense that it was my fault. 

From looking at the discourse around this game, it seems like the community has been divided between those looking for a casual, fun way to spend a few hours finding cool synergies, and those looking for a very precise, very challenging technical game requiring a deep understanding of the intricacies of card interacti…

After putting 150 hours in Slay the Spire, I expected more from Slay the Spire 2. While the new characters and cards are very interesting and add much needed variety, the scaling of the enemies/bosses has gone way up to the point where it's not fun. It seems that all the frustrating aspects of Slay the Spire were amplified in its sequel. While in the first game the aggravating moments where present, they were not coloring the whole run. However in Slay the Spire 2, you will run into intense debuffs and annoying mechanics almost every battle. 

The biggest problem is the amount of statuses the enemies inflict making the game truly unplayable at times. The reduction off strength and dexterity being slapped onto every elite and boss; the statuses dealing increased damage compared to its predecessor; the amount of CARDS being added with those. 

In addition, the damage has gone way up but the base defense has not. I have never been this starved for hp in the first game, as I have been in this game, even playing a block build. 

Overall, I cannot recommend this game at this point of EA. I will continue playing with new updates, hopefully this review will change into the positive. I'm looking forward to the future of this game and excited to conquer the Spire once more.

Only thing that has improved from first is the art. The game is frustrating, it started off fine. But more unlocks I got, the worst the experience got. There is so many debuffs you can consider your damage and block nerfed at all times. The debuffs never go away, and standard enemies are honestly more dangerous than elites. They will routinely deal more damage than you can block in the first turn, you will always be subject to damage no matter how well you manage your cards. You can pick all or none, it doesn't seem to be making tangible difference. Enemy health, damage and buffs/debuffs are excessive. Combats will easily drag on and it ends up feeling like I am expected to one shot everything off the bat. 

Now if you do enjoy surviving on one health even basic encounters and promptly dying next then it is definitely a masterpiece. However as a balanced experience it's horrid baseline and I cannot imagine what the additional difficulty modifiers will look like. It's grueling to the point it's not fun and there is no way for skill to save you here, no making best of the worst. It's so bad I think it'd genuinely be a better experience if the entire game was first turn where you get pummeled to death by the first enemies and nothing else. No cards, no turn based combat, just that.

I've played this game fr 55 hours and 54 of them were with friends! it's a great game to play together
Great game, love playing with friends
its just so flippin well made, and the multiplayer is the best thing ever, trying to beat acension 10 with your buddies feels like a proper adventure beyond the horizons

Overall StS2 is a improvement on StS (which I have been playing on the PS5).  The updates to the core mechanics are subtle, but good and the UI tweaks make it easier to play - little but useful things, like the 'End Turn' button flashes red if there are still cards that can be played.
The biggest improvement though is multi-player, which was much better than anticipated, and a whole lot of fun to play with three other people.

If you like deck building games you know this title is a staple of the genre. it's fun to reach the top of the spire, with increasing difficulty and different games modes. the co-op mode is what makes it the best, there are unique cards you can only use there and they're wicked awesome. it's a chill game you can play while watching something in the background but also there's story for each character, so pay attention. Enjoy!
Incredible game. Builds off the first one and makes it better. Multiplayer is a blast and it's one of the best coop experences out there.
If you liked Slay the Spire, you'll probably like Slay the Spire 2. I've been really enjoying the early access build so far. I've especially enjoyed the multiplayer!
Extremely addicting and very reminiscent of the boardgame. Love the multiplayer aspect, and the ascensions are very fun!

For me, Slay the Spire 2 is so much more addictive than the first game! I love deck-building games, but am still a newbie to the strategy, and it's very inclusive to experimenting and goofing around. Love the different cost/benefit techniques of the Regent, the Necrobinder and the Silent in particular. The co-op with other players is also exceptional! Tl;dr: Join the obsession...we can take down the Heart together...

A great expansion on the first Slay the Spire game, with two full new decks being added.  While I'm not normally not a fan of early access experiences, I appreciate the way that Mega Crit is using this opportunity to collect community feedback and improve the final product.  I wouldn't recommend buying the game at full price at this time, unless you're interested in taking part in that development process.  

I've really enjoyed the game, and already gotten a lot of time out of the beta, but ultimately wouldn't be giving it a positive review based on the current game state, if I wasn't confident that it will continue to improve and progress.  The player decks and bosses still need further fine tuning and balancing.  That being said, it's already well ahead of a lot of other deck builder rogue likes on the market, and have already reached ascension ten on my favorite deck.  I do hope they'll add additional ascension or difficulty modifiers as the game approaches release.  

Additionally, co op is a massive value add for the game.  I would pay the full price just for those features alone.

This game is insanely addictive. 45 hours of my current 59 hours have been co-op. I enjoyed the original game, but the co-op really makes this game for me. Watching a youtube video on the left monitor, chatting with friends in discord, doing a side project… all while Slaying The Spire on the main monitor! 9/10 game, recommended whether you have friends, or if you don’t!
Excellent game! Best enjoyed with friends. Expect saltiness and random heroics.

The devs focused on creating an overly punishing game. The Act3 bosses imo(especially test subject) feel like a paranoid solution to the very fun synergies that are provided. Really disappointing and feels like the game is catered to hardcore players/streamers. Multiplayer is still incredible to play with friends though.

This game is the previous game, with slightly more content.
Until the developer figures out better game balance, I can't recommend getting it for any reason other than co-op. If you don't want to play StS co-op, then you're better off downloading mods for the previous game.
still the same feel as the first game But more cards, more characters, and more Fun. The fact that it is now multiplayer makes it even better a great game to just chill and play with friends!

Slay the spire 2 is a 'okay' sequel to slay the spire 1 at the time of writing

Single player runs are alright, mainly the daily runs.

But this game suffers from 'people played the first one too much so we need to tune around them'

The enemies are all the same variation of endlessly scalling strength, debuffing your stats, or status cards out the ass. (instead of the general probe of weaknesses that StS1 enemies have)

Also the multiplayer scaling for 2-3 players is absolute ass, the scaling is basicly built around needing everyone to be optimal and sharing the same braincells, if someone misplays? runs dead, even on A0 runs.

Wait for the devs to actually tune the game, or just go play StS1 or any other inspired game of the same genre.

it is a super fun deck building, rogue-like rpg. If u like games like Balatro then this is a game for u. If your concerned its not worth buying because u already have the first, it definitely is. It has way better graphics, new mechanics and character and all around is better. Also the multiplayer function is super cool and works really well.

At the time of writing, this game is still in early access. It's a STELLAR game already. I love the art they've done, and also the placeholder art for epochs they're still working on. The ascensions are challenging, the enemies are interesting, and I like the balancing so far with relics and different deck builds. Each character is remarkably distinct, so the game never really gets old (at least, so far). I can't wait to see how the game changes as they continue updating!

I will say, I prefer multiplayer bc singleplayer feels SO much more difficult in comparison. I win probably 6/10 games I play with one or more friends, but I win like....1 out of every 5-7 solo games. It's a bit tricky when there's no potion sharing, no one to help u apply debuffs, etc. So maybe there needs to be some more balancing in the singplayer mode so it doesn't feel impossible for most runs.
A slightly better roguelike game that you can play either solo or with friends. If you're into DnD, this is for you! (Without other elements such as rolling a dice)

I played a lot of months ago, reached Ascension 9 and had a really good time with the game altough the hero strength was kinda unbalanced. Started to play the game some days ago and after several hours i have to say that whatever the devs did in the last couple months they completely broken the enemy balance without even fixing the unbalance between the heroes in the first place. I tackled the high ascensions before but now even lower ascensions are difficult af. Easier elites were changed/buffed to be more diffucult then even the more difficult ones before. Some normal enemies are stronger then some elites and they buffed the base dmg of most enemies. You often start the game and can't possibly win the early fights without already sustaining alot of dmg which just sucks all fun out of the game. They changed many mechanics that wren't broken in the first place and made them player unfriendly. I didnt believe the bad reviews at first but after the last couple hours it was more than obvious that they buffed the enemies alot and made the game just unfun. Don't buy the game they had a gem and ruined the experience completely unnecessarily. For now i think i will go back to the first game. That's atleast player friendly, respects your time and is balanced.

The devs focused on creating an overly punishing game. The Act3 bosses imo(especially test subject) feel like a paranoid solution to the very fun synergies that are provided. Really disappointing and feels like the game is catered to hardcore players/streamers. Multiplayer is still incredible to play with friends though.

Game gets unbearably unbalanced in the later ascensions. Characters get stale after a few runs and they dont seem to be adding more. The pure mental torture of going through asc nine for an hour just to get one shot by uncounterable bosses. You can have an absolutely perfect run and a god tier setup and the game still screws you over with rng. Honestly don't waste your time getting addicted to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

Addition: Game continues to have horrid balancing on final bosses on asc9-10 . Completely uncounterable. Withers that dont exhaust strength, that goes up with every card played. Completely random if you win a run or not ngl, the runs you do end up winning feel like they gave it to you.

Too unbalanced and random in its current state, as a person who loved the first game this sequel has taken away some of what i felt the first game excelled in. The rewards for beating bosses have been knocked down from very strong relics to a choice of three cards like any common enemy, the fun variety and playstyle diversity of the first game has been dumbed down to "get infinite block, godly card cycling and high damage every turn or die before the third act", the elite enemies and even some normal enemies feel highly overtuned, and overall the difficulty feels more random and annoying than the fun challenge of it's predecessor. And as much as i'd like to chalk this up to "skill issue", even good players can't consistently win with the level of randomness and unbalance. Hopefully these issues are smoothed out in the full release

claims.claim: Act 1 is front-loaded and difficult, with enemies dealing high damage before players can draft enough cards.

citations.review_text: My only major issue with the game comes down to Act 1 is far too front-loaded—enemies deal way too much damage before you’ve had a chance to draft enough cards to build a viable deck. After 500+ hours and beating steam://launch/2868840/DialogAscension 10 on every character, I feel like I've spent 80% of my total playtime stuck grinding through the first act.

TLDR: Slay the Spire 2 is exactly what a Slay the Spire 1 fan would want in a sequel: it keeps the spirit of the original while making it both more challenging and more rewarding. 

Slay the Spire (StS) was foundational to the now massive Deckbuilding-Roguelike genre and few games have come close to competing (looking at you Balatro). So when they released Slay the Spire 2 (StS2) I was skeptical. StS still held my heart for the feel of Deckbuilding Roguelikes and so many have failed to iterate in a way that wouldn't fade with novelty. And then I played my first run.
I had heard from friends who were Hollow Knight fans how amazing Silksong was to play even with all the hype and expectations. With StS2, I get it personally now. As someone who generally played in the low to to mid 10s ascensions in StS, StS2 rocked my world. Act 1 was much more of a threat even at base difficulty.  The enemies were more complex with more numbers and multi-hits. These were foes you couldn't just stall out and win without a scratch. 
But to combat this, our favorite characters (sorry Watcher) came back stronger than ever. Ironclads had better block cards and more ruthless attacks.  Silent can throw more knives, the poison doubling is a power happens every turn, and still can tank powerful boss attacks to the face. Defect gets more lighting channeling, actual darkness support, mixed orb builds are entirely viable, power builds are even more powerful and claw is still law. These characters feel like they have faced the original spire over and over again and came back with its shattered heart. The new characters are nothing to snub at either. Regent has a secondary mana resource that actually feels fun to use and can make the biggest sword. Necrobinder has a single summon but actually interacts well with it and has other fun and unique mechanics with doom, etherial, and souls. And to top it all off, the colorless cards are actually good across the spectrum.
Sure, it'll take a number of…

claims.claim: Multiplayer scaling is unbalanced and difficult for two-player sessions, leading to high wipe rates against final bosses.

citations.review_text:
I hate to leave a mixed review on this game, because it has the potential to be a lot of fun. Unfortunately, I have to leave this warning to co-op players: don't even bother if you're trying 2-player.

My wife and I have logged dozens of attempts together, and we're generally pretty good at co-op games. STS2 is HORRIBLY unbalanced with two players; we've made it to the final boss a single time and stood zero chance. It's quickly losing the appeal of even making more attempts. This is a known balance issue and has been for some time, but the devs don't seem to be making any tweaks. I don't feel like finding a third or fourth player just for the sake of finishing the game, and it's not really my cup of tea solo. We've tried every combination of characters, different deck builds, synergizing, doing our own thing; nothing makes it feel substantially easier, only RNG.

What we have is a fun and polished-looking game that has been surrounded and crushed with confusing, terrible decisions. The one thing Slay The Spire 2 has over its predecessor is functional multiplayer, except it's absolutely impossible to play higher ascensions with friends.

Every enemy has numbers that are simply far too high and don't match up to your own cards. Too much health, too much damage, too many buffs. Certain enemies are far easier to deal with if you have specific characters on your team, and if you don't have them, you will almost certainly wipe. There has been an ongoing problem with the Act 3 Bosses being unfun and overtuned for months now. There are multiple enemies that are so powerful they qualify as elites, but they AREN'T elite fights, and can end your run easily.

Almost every time I've asked for help from the STS community, I'm simply told I'm whining and that I have to get better. The game isn't at fault - it's mine, for not having better RNG, and not knowing meta card combos, and not having 500 hours of experience with deckbuilders. Because god forbid I just want to have fun. Even the easiest difficulty is like a pressure wash for my brain.

Wait for the 1.0 release. It's just not worth it with the way they keep nerfing things that were fine and buffing things that don't need buffing just because the developers are obsessed with creating a masochistic card game to weed out the weak. Hopefully by then they'll at least have added a difficulty more suited for fun than challenge.

claims.claim: The Act 3 boss Aeonglass adds an unmanageable number of Wither status cards and has excessive health, making runs heavily dependent on specific counters.

citations.review_text: I cannot recommend this game until the act 3 boss, Aeonglass, is nerfed or removed. You lose runs just from the boss existing. Doesn't matter if you pick up cards that exhaust its wither cards. It will always add more withers than what you can deal with. Unless you're playing the defect and high-roll flak cannon every run, you will lose to Aeonglass most of the time. You are simply outscaled in damage to kill it.

Aeonglass is the worst thing you ever made. 
Not because its just "too hard", ive beaten it many times on A10, but because of how disproportionately more annoying than anything else in the game it is.

You could have a run where you breeze through Act 3 without taking damage or resting and still get mathmatically stomped with 0 counterplay because you could only build a deck with the "wrong" playstyle (playing many cards without much exhaust).
On the other hand with single big damage cards and exhaust like Ironclad its laughably easy and boring. It limits variety and turns many runs into pure gambling. (get aeon = lose, dont get aeon = win)

Doormaker had some similar problems too but the phases gave you some options to play smart and still win.
Please change it back or just make another boss.

I personally am a big fan of the game and it's potential but it definitely has some flaws. For a start the RNG is sometimes questionable and some runs can just be not winnable. This feels especially true on higher Ascension runs where it might take 30 tries to win a single run on A10. There is also the issue with the bosses of Act 3. I think the Queen is actually pretty well balanced and beatable if you have a decent build. Test Subject is a nightmare in multiplayer for his first phase. The devs should try to mold his mechanic around how current Infested Prim is with Tainted to negate the damage momentum and to prevent your allies from accidentally killing you turn one. It would still be harsh but actually bearable, specifically in multiplayer. Aeonglass just sucks. Withers already held in your deck shouldn't be upgraded and due to it's monstrous health it will usually take a while to bring his health down and by that point you might draw 3 withers all dealing 9 damage basically dooming. Despite all of this however, I am optimistic about the game's future, especially with modding coming in. The game does have great replayability  and each character has multiple build options that are viable and fun. The general mechanics of the game are good and the RNG has been improving as the devs take note it. With the promise of a fourth act and more characters I think the game can have a great future as long as the underlined issues are addressed.

A really solid foundation and pretty much what you'd expect from a great sequel, only to be held back by the currently poor balancing of Ascension 9+ and Aeonglass. 

Ascension 9 is so overkill that even with your best min-maxing, RNG holds the biggest factor for success and you will probably lose 90-95% of A9-A10 runs, way too overkill compared to A20 runs from StS1, which I comfortably did A20 runs on every character in.

Then there's Aeonglass. This boss is just beyond broken and at this point I'd rather have the door boss back. It isn't even a fun or interesting boss, just raw damage output, artifact defense, card play punishment, and ridiculous status card scaling. Right now there is no point in even attempting this boss on higher Ascensions.

Will change review once Mega Crit learns how to balance the game better.

Writing this primarily because of the recent Aeonglass changes.
Doormaker may have split the community, but it mostly only punished a specific intentional style of deckbuilding, which was pretty cheesy to begin with(ultra-slim decks with OP infinites). 

I hadn't played for a while and came back to a run(A6 Necrobinder), and faced Aeonglass after the changes to Wither made them unplayable. It's honestly BS, the fix is basically 'play a different character, or specifically employ a strategy that is only 1 way of playing the character/game, and know it ahead of time before you get to A3'. I even looked for Exhaust or Discard cards right at the beginning of A3, and happened to have several hundred gold, the Discount Card relic, and hit 3 shops before fighting the boss. No cards to help. I had an extremely strong deck, with excellent damage, tons of card draw, energy relics, etc I went into the fight with a Dexterity Potion and Powdered Demise, and I had full Health. Wither being unplayable is just ridiculous, especially with the way it scales. 

It makes me not even want to play the game anymore. Game is just turning into 'play it this one specific way or lose, also hope for RNG, and just fail runs until you get ultra-lucky RNG win'. Invalidating skilled play, deck construction, and knowledge with cheap mechanics that require hyperspecific decisions to overcome entirely removes player agency, and it sucks.

We had a 3 stack of some of the strongest builds in the game against the hour glass at ASCENSION 5 perfect dagger build perfect iron clad blood loss build and strong status build in defect. Now we cant enjoy a run we get crazy builds see him and death in 6 turns. Atleast the door maker gave you a chance. i love this game but this guy belongs in ascension 10 as the second boss. Your casual 200 hour player cant even make a attempt. If this is how your gonna make it for the normal players this wont be a game i keep playing. Id fight 2 act 3 bosses back to back than deal with this crap in multiplayer. solo he is a great boss but 2000 health on a enemy that stacks wither into your hand on top of 50 damage swings and 130 shield. Really

claims.claim: Certain non-elite enemies like Skulking Colony and Infested Prism heavily punish specific archetypes and skill-based card decks.

citations.review_text:
As much as I want to like the game, as of today, I don't recommend this game as a solo experience (multiplayer is fun though).

Most of the changes to the game these past few months have felt like the devs are actively trying to increase the amount of frustration there is in any given run, and the best way to deal with most mechanics is ignore them and end the encounter in less than 4 turns. Every enemy on every floor feels like a differently flavoured damage race, instead of an active interplay between the enemy and your deck. 
Worse yet, a lot of the fights that feel like they would reward a more consistent deck end up either getting changed in the beta branch (e.g. Skulking Colony) or have some sort of scaling mechanic in a fight where you're asked to deal with 20+ damage per turn regularly (e.g. Phantasmal Killer). Slay 2 is quite a fast paced game on average (at least compared to its predecessor), but it doesn't feel like an organic change of pace. Rather, it's because if the player doesn't have a fast enough deck, they just get crushed.

Character decks feel very interesting, and synergies feel satisfying, but the fun I derive from actually playing a fight out gets sapped by numerous mechanics that feel overly punishing, especially to certain characters and archetypes (e.g. Vantom, Hunter Killer, Entomancer, new Infested Prism, 2 Chompers, Aeonglass, etc.).
Further, because enemies are overly punishing to slower decks, the player is heavily incentivised to have a very slim deck for consistency, which means less opportunity to take more cards for fun and branch out to try new cards. 
This is on top of the devs nerfing the ability of the player to draw cards basically every time they make a change. Infinites were a problem that feel like they got addressed pretty quickly, and rightly so, but now it just feels like it's intended design to just regularly dead draw if the size of the player's deck is any more than 20 cards. More enemies have debilitating punishes t…

This game is still early access which means they can turn it around. But they seem to be suffering from their own success and the balance changes seem geared toward removing player agency more than actual balance. They're probably focusing more on their future board game than making actual gameplay toward decision-making for their player base.

And for a roguelike, that's unacceptable. Why is resting at a campfire 99% of the time the best option before a major fight? Why are the most obvious card picks so pigeonholed?

Let me elaborate on that point. The Underdocks is a great example. I'm encouraged because of the enemies here to turtle for 2/3 of the elites as taking terrible attacks just leads me to be punished. Skulking colony limits how much damage you can do per turn and Phantasmal Gardners get block whenever you attack them. So for Ironclad, you either turtle until you have scaling, or vuln set up; for silent, poison; for Defect, damage orbs; for Necrobinder, doom; and for Regent, colorless/strength scaling. This is easiest way in general because of the lack of energy generation and mostly done through skills which give you the added benefit of block.

These SAME strategies are punished so hard in Act 2. Decimillipede and Infested Prism (especially the new one) laugh at your attempts to build any of the above I just mentioned. Did Book of Stabbing in StS, or Gremlin Leader, or Slavers care if you built in a specific way to play? No, as long as you had a balanced deck to block and have offense, you weren't directly punished for building in a certain way.

And that's the crux of the issue with this. I get there are people that are mass downvoting because they're upset with Doormaker, or Aeonglass, or whatever the next iteration of enemies are. And maybe that criticism is unjustified. But for those that are genuinely complaining that they can't make choices? Where are the changes that reflect those comments? They seem to only care about steering the game to how T…

I recommend the game, *but not in its current state for higher challenge players*
I'll also preface this by saying I don't watch people play this game. That does nothing for me and I am comfortable speaking to my own experience compared to the first game (beat A20 on switch, all achievements)  and that of my friends, rather than "what defines the meta" or however people talk about this. 

I know I could be way better. Just trying to speak to the experience of a casual player who maybe has 3 or 4 days a month to sit down and game for an evening. 

Generally love this game and I recognize we are still in early access, but I have to call it soon after the recent waves of changes. I don't have time to keep adapting to card changes, making a pick and then realizing it is a completely different card, and elite and boss changes that feel like spaghetti stuck on a wall, but gradually sliding down to make room for less sticky spaghetti. I'm glad I supported the project and had a ton of fun at the initial release. I regret nothing, but I honestly just want people to wait until its done so they don't leave with a sour taste in their throats. 

Generally I'm talking about A8-10 here, but it also extends to the game as a whole. 
Not a fan of aeonglass. Not a fan of the demon dorito. Generally, there seems to be a hyperfixation on enemies that swing every turn, punishing skill card based decks to balance silent and necrobinder, but those decks adapt better. The regent and the defect can't as well, especially the defect in multiplayer. 
Also not a fan of the curve in act 1. Still feels sad to see all the tools for an incredible build except 1, and then come across some of the higher difficulty fights in a chain, and watch a unique opportunity die. The filter could be shifted to act 3 floors, which is often a cakewalk by comparison until the boss. 

It just generally feels like the game introduced more mechanics, and then punishes you for trying to explore ways to use new cards and…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the Act 3 boss Aeonglass is extremely difficult, adding Wither cards into the player's deck and scaling to cause run losses.

citations.review_text: I cannot recommend this game until the act 3 boss, Aeonglass, is nerfed or removed. You lose runs just from the boss existing. Doesn't matter if you pick up cards that exhaust its wither cards. It will always add more withers than what you can deal with. Unless you're playing the defect and high-roll flak cannon every run, you will lose to Aeonglass most of the time. You are simply outscaled in damage to kill it.

Aeonglass is the worst thing you ever made. 
Not because its just "too hard", ive beaten it many times on A10, but because of how disproportionately more annoying than anything else in the game it is.

You could have a run where you breeze through Act 3 without taking damage or resting and still get mathmatically stomped with 0 counterplay because you could only build a deck with the "wrong" playstyle (playing many cards without much exhaust).
On the other hand with single big damage cards and exhaust like Ironclad its laughably easy and boring. It limits variety and turns many runs into pure gambling. (get aeon = lose, dont get aeon = win)

Doormaker had some similar problems too but the phases gave you some options to play smart and still win.
Please change it back or just make another boss.
